sections.h2: Paying the bill and finding the right office
sections.html:
Chattooga's Tax Commissioner handles billing and collection and has no say in values or millage. The Board of Tax Assessors, appointed by the county commissioner, appraises property and approves every exemption claimed. A Board of Equalization chosen by the Grand Jury hears appeals. Rates are set by the county commissioner for county tax and by the Board of Education for school tax.

  • Location: Courthouse Annex, 120 Cox Street, Summerville, GA 30747. Mail: P.O. Box 517, Summerville, GA 30747-0517.
  • Phone 706-857-0703. The office is open 7:30 AM to 5:30 PM Monday through Friday, except that it is closed on Wednesdays.
  • Bills can be searched and paid online at chattoogacountytax.com.
  • Mailed payments count with a United States Postal Service postmark but not with a metered one.

Bills go to the homeowner and only sometimes to the mortgage company, so pass yours to the lender if your taxes are escrowed.

Chattooga sits in Georgia's northwest corner, with 314 square miles and Summerville as the seat. Trion, Lyerly and Menlo are the other cities. Several county properties are on national historic registers, which can matter because Georgia offers preferential assessment for qualifying historic buildings.

The 2025 estimate is 25,300 residents, near the 24,965 counted in 2020. For 2020 to 2024 a typical owner-held home is worth $115,600, typical rent is $790 and 66.8% of homes are owner-occupied. Only 2 building permits were issued in 2025.

December 1 is the usual deadline for land, buildings and business equipment. Interest begins the next day, and a 5% penalty is added after 120 days. A homesteaded parcel owing less than $500 avoids the 120-day penalty. Mobile and manufactured homes are due April 1, with 1% interest added each month they are late.

The Tax Commissioner calls a levy a last resort, but unpaid taxes can be levied on. Once a bill is more than 30 days late, a tax FiFa (lien) can be entered in the Superior Court clerk's records. Those entries are public, credit bureaus may use them, and the tax office has no control over that.

Excess funds from past tax sales are listed on the Tax Commissioner's website, so a former owner can check whether money is waiting.

State exemptions are listed by the Tax Commissioner, along with local ones that replace the state amount when larger. You must own the home and live in it on January 1, and the application goes to the Tax Assessor's Office. You can file all year, but only an application in hand by April 1 takes effect that year.

Chattooga County homestead exemptions
ExemptionWho qualifiesWhat it does
StandardAny qualifying homeowner$2,000 off the 40% assessed value; excludes bond levies
Standard elderly schoolAge 62 or older, net income at most $10,000Up to $10,000 off assessed value, school tax only
Standard elderly generalAge 65 or older, net income at most $10,000Up to $4,000 off assessed value for county, school and state
Local countyAge 70 or older, federal adjusted gross income at most $20,000Sliding 20% to 100% share of assessed value, county tax only, for the residence and up to 5 acres
Local schoolAge 70 or older, same income limitUp to $40,000 of assessed value, school tax only
FloatingAge 62 or older, household income at most $30,000State and county tax, not school; replaces other exemptions

The floating exemption can raise a bill at first, since it replaces other state and county exemptions already in place. Disabled owners with a service-connected disability have their own exemption, and so do unremarried widows of service members killed in armed conflict and of firefighters or peace officers who died on duty.

Owners 62 or older with gross household income up to $15,000 can defer, but not escape, tax on a homestead. The deferred amount generally stays due until ownership changes or the deferred taxes plus interest reach 85% of fair market value, which means a sale usually triggers repayment from proceeds.

  • Agricultural land in bona fide farming can be assessed at 30% instead of 40%, and conservation use property is valued at its current use. Both require a covenant to keep the use for at least 10 years.
  • Qualifying historic buildings can receive preferential assessment on the structure and up to two acres around it.
  • Manufacturers can claim the Freeport exemption on raw goods, goods in process and finished goods awaiting out-of-state shipment, by applying with the Board of Tax Assessors between January 1 and April 1.

sections.h2: How to contest a Chattooga County value
sections.html:
You have 45 days from the notice date. The appeal goes first to the assessors, who look at their value again. If you remain unhappy, the next stop is the Board of Equalization or an arbitrator, and a final written notice sent or filed with the assessors carries the case to Superior Court.

Grounds are taxability, value, or uniformity compared with neighboring properties. A complaint that the tax is too high does not qualify, since the county commissioner and Board of Education set that. Mobile home owners who dispute a revised value have 30 days to reach the Board of Equalization.

Returns are accepted until April 1. After a first return, real property returns carry forward unless something changes, but personal property returns are needed every year.

Whoever holds title on January 1 owes tax for the full year, and there is no refund for part-year owners. The closing attorney should divide the year on the settlement statement.

Your exemption stays behind with you, and a purchaser moving in must file by April 1. If you need a copy of a deed for the closing file, the Clerk of Superior Court keeps a deed room in the Chattooga County Courthouse. With homes priced around $115,600, even a modest unpaid balance and penalty can weigh on a sale, so pull a payoff early.

Because the tax office is closed on Wednesdays, plan your calls and visits for the other weekdays, or use chattoogacountytax.com to look up the bill. Ask for a written payoff, and ask whether any older year is open. If the house is a mobile or manufactured home, check the April 1 account separately, since it runs apart from the December bill.

Give the payoff to the closing attorney early. A cash buyer expects the same documents as any other buyer, and a clean payoff is what keeps a lien from slowing the sale.

faqs.q: What is the usual Chattooga County deadline?
faqs.a: December 1 for land, buildings and business equipment. Mobile and manufactured homes run on an April 1 schedule.

faqs.q: Can I visit the Chattooga tax office on a Wednesday?
faqs.a: No. The Tax Commissioner's office is closed on Wednesdays and open 7:30 AM to 5:30 PM the other weekdays.

faqs.q: How costly is a late payment in Chattooga County?
faqs.a: Interest starts the day after the due date. A 5% penalty applies after 120 days, except for homesteaded property with liability under $500.

faqs.q: Does a Chattooga County homestead exemption need yearly renewal?
faqs.a: No. Once granted it renews automatically unless you move, change ownership or want a different exemption, and the deadline for a first application is April 1.

faqs.q: How do I find a deed copy for a Chattooga County property?
faqs.a: Ask the Superior Court clerk, whose deed room is in the Chattooga County Courthouse.
